summary: Backend-only testing of CourtBazaar. Created comprehensive pytest suite (38 tests) covering health, auth (login/register/OTP), profile, courts, services, files, orders, payments, AI, subscriptions, wallet, vendor flow, vendor onboarding, admin flow and auth security. 37/38 tests passed. Fixed a real ObjectId serialization bug in /api/auth/otp/verify. Only failure is /api/ai/filing-checklist due to EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget exhausted (external, not a code bug).

critical.issue: Emergent LLM key budget exceeded: 'Current cost: 0.006, Max budget: 0.001'. Filing checklist consistently returns 500. AI chat passed once but will fail on next call. Backend logs: 'litellm.BadRequestError: Budget has been exceeded'. Likely budget cap on the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in backend/.env.

minor.issue: FIXED during testing: returned 500 ('ObjectId is not iterable') when creating a brand-new user via OTP because the inserted document still contained the Mongo _id ObjectId when being serialized. Added user.pop('_id', None) after insert_one, identical to the pattern already used in /auth/register.

Returns a dict (object keyed by plan_id), not a JSON list. Functionally correct (4 plans present) but the review request asked for 'returns 4 plans' — frontend should iterate Object.entries(). Consider returning a list of {plan_id, name, price, features} for cleaner API contract.
Stores session in cookie with samesite=none, secure=true. Works behind HTTPS preview URL but will not work in plain HTTP local dev. Not blocking.

action_items: Investigate/refresh EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget — current cap is $0.001 which is exhausted after 1-2 requests. AI Chat & Filing Checklist features are effectively broken in production. This is the highest-priority fix.
Consider returning /api/subscriptions/plans as a list with explicit plan_id for cleaner contract (optional).
Re-test /api/ai/* endpoints after the LLM key/budget is restored.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 926 lines and contains every domain (auth, courts, services, files, orders, payments, AI, admin, subscriptions, wallet). Should be split into /app/backend/routes/{auth,orders,payments,...}.py modules; an empty /app/backend/routes/ folder already exists. >700 line rule violated.

Several endpoints (POST /orders, vendor_onboard, get_order, etc.) duplicate the pattern of 'find_one without _id projection, then pop _id'. Standardize on always projecting {'_id': 0} in find_one to avoid future serialization regressions (the OTP bug fixed today was exactly this).

/api/auth/me, /api/orders, /api/vendors/me, etc. enforce auth via Depends(get_current_user) — good. However, /api/files/upload trusts file.filename without validation; suggest size limit & content-type allowlist (PDF/PNG/JPG) to prevent abuse.

/api/orders/{id}/status allows any vendor token to update if vendor_id matches — but a 'vendor' role with a DIFFERENT vendor_id is also allowed by the OR check `user['role'] not in ('admin','vendor')`. The condition should be: admin OR (vendor AND order.vendor_id == user.user_id). Currently any vendor can update any order's status.
AI endpoints use streaming but block on full response — set a hard timeout / max_tokens to prevent 502s on long generations.
Stripe webhook (/api/webhook/stripe) silently catches all exceptions and returns ok:true — should at least log and return 400 for invalid signatures so Stripe retries are sane.

rca of the issue: Filing checklist failure RCA: litellm.BadRequestError raised by emergentintegrations -> Budget exceeded (Max budget: 0.001, current 0.006). Reproduction: POST /api/ai/filing-checklist with {court:'Tis Hazari', case_type:'Civil Suit'} using advocate token. Mitigation: increase/refresh the budget for EMERGENT_LLM_KEY or rotate the key. The first /api/ai/chat call sometimes succeeds because each request has independent cost accounting only when budget head-room exists; subsequent calls in the same hour will 500. OTP verify RCA (already fixed): insert_one mutated the dict to inject ObjectId _id; FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize ObjectId -> 500. Fix: pop _id after insert (consistent with /auth/register).
